guides.title: Multiple myeloma
guides.description: Selected myeloma repurposing research, separating experimental anticancer mechanisms from clot prevention and established treatment context.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. It can damage bone and interfere with healthy blood-cell production. Thalidomide is an example of repurposing that reached an approved cancer indication. This is a selected-source overview of investigated interventions, not a complete survey of every repurposed drug for myeloma. Experimental tumor studies and clot-prevention research answer different questions.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The selected experimental candidates below remain distinct from established myeloma treatment. Their laboratory effects do not determine which treatment a patient should receive.

questions.question: Is thalidomide an investigational myeloma treatment?
questions.answer: Its combination with dexamethasone has an established approved indication. The appropriate regimen still depends on the patient’s disease and treatment context.

sentences.text: Its combination with dexamethasone has an established approved indication. The appropriate regimen still depends on the patient’s disease and treatment context.

questions.question: What does metformin evidence show?
questions.answer: Clinical evidence: Low. Metformin inhibited myeloma-cell growth and mouse xenograft growth, with AMPK activation, mTOR-pathway changes, autophagy and cell-cycle arrest. The cell experiments did not show apoptosis. These model findings do not establish tumor control or survival benefit in patients.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Low. Metformin inhibited myeloma-cell growth and mouse xenograft growth, with AMPK activation, mTOR-pathway changes, autophagy and cell-cycle arrest. The cell experiments did not show apoptosis. These model findings do not establish tumor control or survival benefit in patients.

questions.question: What was tested with itraconazole?
questions.answer: Clinical evidence: Low. Itraconazole with arsenic trioxide reduced myeloma-cell growth and tumor burden in mouse experiments, with lower GLI1-related Hedgehog signaling. This combination evidence cannot establish itraconazole-alone benefit or a human myeloma regimen.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Low. Itraconazole with arsenic trioxide reduced myeloma-cell growth and tumor burden in mouse experiments, with lower GLI1-related Hedgehog signaling. This combination evidence cannot establish itraconazole-alone benefit or a human myeloma regimen.

questions.question: What does simvastatin evidence show?
questions.answer: Clinical evidence: Low. Simvastatin reduced viability in myeloma cell lines. Cell-cycle effects and the type of cell death differed between lines. An in vitro effect does not establish an effective anticancer dose or benefit in people.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Thalidomide can cause severe birth defects and blood clots. Nerve damage is another clinically important risk of this drug class; these hazards are integral to treatment selection and monitoring.

This is human supportive-care evidence, not a test of aspirin as an antimyeloma drug. Different treatment purposes cannot be pooled into one cancer-benefit estimate.

faqs.question: Why can myeloma cause bone and blood problems?
faqs.answer: Abnormal plasma cells accumulate in bone marrow, interfering with normal blood-cell production and contributing to bone damage.

sentences.text: Abnormal plasma cells accumulate in bone marrow, interfering with normal blood-cell production and contributing to bone damage.

guides.title: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome
guides.description: ME/CFS repurposing evidence: patient-derived immune-cell findings, anecdotal naltrexone responses and unresolved clinical questions.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms. Naltrexone research has examined altered signaling in natural-killer immune cells as one possible treatment target.

sentences.text: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms.
Naltrexone research has examined altered signaling in natural-killer immune cells as one possible treatment target.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low for symptom benefit. The TRPM3 study examined natural-killer cells from nine people with ME/CFS already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls. Channel currents resembled those in healthy-control cells. There was no randomized treated-versus-untreated ME/CFS comparison measuring recovery, daily function or post-exertional malaise. Clinical evidence: Low. Three published patient-compiled case histories described variable symptom changes during naltrexone use. One reported better pain and sleep without improved function. Self-selection, retrospective reporting, other treatments and illness fluctuation prevent a causal response estimate; these cases do not establish a validated ME/CFS dose.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Low for symptom benefit. The TRPM3 study examined natural-killer cells from nine people with ME/CFS already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls. Channel currents resembled those in healthy-control cells. There was no randomized treated-versus-untreated ME/CFS comparison measuring recovery, daily function or post-exertional malaise.

Clinical evidence: Low. Three published patient-compiled case histories described variable symptom changes during naltrexone use. One reported better pain and sleep without improved function. Self-selection, retrospective reporting, other treatments and illness fluctuation prevent a causal response estimate; these cases do not establish a validated ME/CFS dose.

questions.question: Has this research shown that naltrexone restores daily function?
questions.answer: No controlled clinical improvement can be estimated from this cell study. Its finding concerns ion-channel behavior, leaving the size and duration of any effect on daily symptoms unanswered.

sentences.text: No controlled clinical improvement can be estimated from this cell study. Its finding concerns ion-channel behavior, leaving the size and duration of any effect on daily symptoms unanswered.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Safety evidence: Low for estimating frequency. Headaches and vivid dreams occurred in the case descriptions. Three reports are too small to characterize uncommon harms, interactions or the safety of a particular low-dose regimen. Official label context: Naltrexone blocks opioid effects and is contraindicated with opioid analgesics or current opioid dependence. It can precipitate severe withdrawal in opioid-dependent people. This product warning is separate from the unproven benefits and dosing of low-dose treatment for ME/CFS.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Cellular channel measurements and patient symptom histories answer different questions. Neither selected report supplies a controlled comparison of clinical benefit.

sentences.text: Cellular channel measurements and patient symptom histories answer different questions. Neither selected report supplies a controlled comparison of clinical benefit.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Clinical benefit: Not established by these selected studies. The case histories and cell findings support further investigation, while comparative response rates, durability and an optimal ME/CFS regimen remain unresolved.

sentences.text: Clinical benefit: Not established by these selected studies. The case histories and cell findings support further investigation, while comparative response rates, durability and an optimal ME/CFS regimen remain unresolved.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The fibromyalgia and Long COVID pages discuss overlapping symptoms in distinct populations; shared fatigue does not make the diagnoses or endpoints identical.

faqs.question: Why can a one-day activity measurement miss an ME/CFS problem?
faqs.answer: Post-exertional malaise can be delayed after activity. Following symptoms over subsequent days can capture deterioration that is not obvious during the activity itself.

sentences.text: Post-exertional malaise can be delayed after activity. Following symptoms over subsequent days can capture deterioration that is not obvious during the activity itself.

faqs.question: What human symptom reports are available?
faqs.answer: Clinical evidence: Low. Three published patient-compiled case histories described variable symptom changes during naltrexone use. One reported better pain and sleep without improved function. Self-selection, retrospective reporting, other treatments and illness fluctuation prevent a causal response estimate; these cases do not establish a validated ME/CFS dose.

faqs.question: What do the case reports establish about safety?
faqs.answer: Safety evidence: Low for estimating frequency. These reports cannot establish uncommon-event risks or a safe dosing schedule.

guides.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
guides.description: Minocycline in ALS: harmful functional trial results, uncertain mortality findings and the limits of a laboratory neuroprotection rationale.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis damages the motor neurons that control voluntary muscles. Progressive weakness can affect movement, speech, swallowing and breathing.

sentences.text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis damages the motor neurons that control voluntary muscles. Progressive weakness can affect movement, speech, swallowing and breathing.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Moderate for harmful functional decline with the tested minocycline regimen. In the randomized 412-person ALS trial, function declined faster than with placebo during nine months. This primary outcome argues against the hoped-for neuroprotective benefit in that setting.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Moderate for harmful functional decline with the tested minocycline regimen. In the randomized 412-person ALS trial, function declined faster than with placebo during nine months. This primary outcome argues against the hoped-for neuroprotective benefit in that setting.

questions.question: How much faster was decline?
questions.answer: ALSFRS-R scores fell by 1.30 points per month with minocycline versus 1.04 with placebo; the difference was statistically significant (P=0.005).

sentences.text: ALSFRS-R scores fell by 1.30 points per month with minocycline versus 1.04 with placebo; the difference was statistically significant (P=0.005).

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Safety evidence: Low for quantifying individual adverse-event risk. Non-serious gastrointestinal and neurological events were more common with minocycline. The abstract did not establish that these events explained the faster functional decline.

sentences.text: Safety evidence: Low for quantifying individual adverse-event risk. Non-serious gastrointestinal and neurological events were more common with minocycline. The abstract did not establish that these events explained the faster functional decline.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Mortality evidence: Low for a difference. Mortality was numerically higher with minocycline, but the estimate was uncertain and not statistically significant. It should not inherit the primary functional outcome's grade or be presented as a proven mortality effect.

sentences.text: Mortality evidence: Low for a difference. Mortality was numerically higher with minocycline, but the estimate was uncertain and not statistically significant. It should not inherit the primary functional outcome's grade or be presented as a proven mortality effect.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The selected trial directly measured function, survival and safety. Its functional-harm assessment applies to the tested regimen; mortality and individual adverse-event risks retain separate uncertainty.

sentences.text: The selected trial directly measured function, survival and safety. Its functional-harm assessment applies to the tested regimen; mortality and individual adverse-event risks retain separate uncertainty.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The minocycline profile brings together its antimicrobial use and the condition-specific results of repurposing trials.

faqs.question: Why are breathing and swallowing outcomes important in ALS?
faqs.answer: ALS can weaken muscles involved in respiration and swallowing as well as the limbs. These functions affect health, communication and daily support needs.

sentences.text: ALS can weaken muscles involved in respiration and swallowing as well as the limbs. These functions affect health, communication and daily support needs.

guides.title: Basal-cell carcinoma
guides.description: Itraconazole in basal cell carcinoma: exploratory human tumor and pathway findings, safety signals and missing long-term outcomes.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sentences.text: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low for short-term tumor-area reduction. Nineteen of 29 enrolled participants received itraconazole in an open-label exploratory study. Tumor area was a secondary assessment in a subset; the result does not establish durable cure, recurrence prevention or superiority to standard local treatment.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Low for short-term tumor-area reduction. Nineteen of 29 enrolled participants received itraconazole in an open-label exploratory study. Tumor area was a secondary assessment in a subset; the result does not establish durable cure, recurrence prevention or superiority to standard local treatment.

questions.question: How much did tumor area change?
questions.answer: Among the treated study participants, mean tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2–30.0%). The study was small and open-label.

sentences.text: Among the treated study participants, mean tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2–30.0%). The study was small and open-label.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Safety evidence: Low for estimating frequency. The small study reported moderate fatigue and a grade 4 congestive-heart-failure event. These observations are important safety signals, but do not define an individual risk or a safe oncology regimen.

sentences.text: Safety evidence: Low for estimating frequency. The small study reported moderate fatigue and a grade 4 congestive-heart-failure event. These observations are important safety signals, but do not define an individual risk or a safe oncology regimen.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: This study does not compare itraconazole with curative local treatment or with approved Hedgehog-pathway drugs.

sentences.text: This study does not compare itraconazole with curative local treatment or with approved Hedgehog-pathway drugs.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low. The short-duration study supports further controlled evaluation, while recurrence, definitive cure and comparison with established local treatment remain unresolved.

sentences.text: Clinical evidence: Low. The short-duration study supports further controlled evaluation, while recurrence, definitive cure and comparison with established local treatment remain unresolved.

faqs.question: Is basal cell carcinoma the same as melanoma?
faqs.answer: No. Basal cell carcinoma arises from basal cells, while melanoma develops from melanocytes. Their biology and treatment evidence are different.

questions.title: Why is immune modulation relevant to myeloma?
questions.text: Myeloma involves malignant plasma cells within a marrow environment that supports their survival. Immunomodulatory treatment acts on cancer-related immune and cellular processes.

questions.title: Is TRPM3 dysfunction established as the single cause of ME/CFS?
questions.text: The study examines one biological pathway. It does not demonstrate that this pathway explains the whole illness or the varied symptoms described in ME/CFS.

questions.text: The signaling measure tests whether the proposed target is affected; tumor area measures a visible cancer response. Neither measurement alone reports long-term recurrence.

sources.population: Three people with longstanding chronic fatigue syndrome; patient-compiled histories
sources.preview: The three cases described variable symptom and functional changes during naltrexone use. Uncontrolled retrospective histories cannot establish causality, a response rate or an optimal dose.
